'''Johan Gielis''' (born July 8, 1962) is a Belgian [[engineer]], [[scientist]], [[mathematician]], and entrepreneur.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Outreach |first=Research |date=2021-09-03 |title=Superellipses to Superformula: The impact of Gielis Transformations |url=https://researchoutreach.org/articles/superellipses-superformula-impact-gielis-transformations/ |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=Research Outreach |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-05-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230526210342/https://researchoutreach.org/articles/superellipses-superformula-impact-gielis-transformations/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Gielis is known for his contributions to the field of mathematics, specifically in the area of modeling and [[Geometry|geometrical methods]]. He is best known for developing the concept of the [[superformula]], which is a generalization of the traditional [[Pythagorean theorem]] and the equation of the circle, that can generate a wide variety of complex shapes found in nature.<ref>{{Cite patent|number=7620527|title=Method and apparatus for synthesizing and analyzing patterns utilizing novel "super-formula" operator|country=US|pubdate=2009-11-17|inventor1-last=Gielis|inventor1-first=Johan Leo Alfons}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gielis obtained a degree in horticultural engineering.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Aitken-Christie |first1=Jenny |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NEbrCAAAQBAJ&dq=who+is+johan+gielis+%3F&pg=PA472 |title=Automation and environmental control in plant tissue culture |last2=Kozai |first2=T. |last3=Smith |first3=M. A. L. |date=2013-06-29 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-94-015-8461-6 |pages=472 |language=en |access-date=2023-07-05 |archive-date=2023-07-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705143154/https://books.google.com/books?id=NEbrCAAAQBAJ&newbks=0&printsec=frontcover&pg=PA472&dq=who+is+johan+gielis+%3F&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref> Later, he changed direction from botany and plant biotechnology to geometry and mathematics.<ref name=":1" /> In 2013, Gielis co founded the Antenna Company, in [[Eindhoven]]. The company applies the [[Superformula|superfomula]] to develop efficient antennas to transmit data via various frequencies.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2020-06-02 |title=How the Gielis Superformula led to an ingenious Caratelli antenna and a modest Dutch start-up that conquered the world |url=https://innovationorigins.com/en/how-the-gielis-superformula-led-to-an-ingenious-caratelli-antenna-and-a-modest-dutch-start-up-that-conquered-the-world/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230323215136/https://innovationorigins.com/en/how-the-gielis-superformula-led-to-an-ingenious-caratelli-antenna-and-a-modest-dutch-start-up-that-conquered-the-world/ |archive-date=2023-03-23 |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=IO |language=en-GB}}</ref> The company made antenna system for ultra-fast [[Wi-Fi 6|WiFi 6]] devices.<ref name=":3" /> Antenna systems focus on 2-7 gigaHertz, in line with the [[Wi-Fi 6|IEEE 802.11ax]] standard and beyond. Other products focus on [[Internet of things|Internet of Things]] and mmWave antenna systems.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Theis |first1=Guilherme |last2=Smolders |first2=A. Bart |last3=Federico |first3=Gabriele |last4=Caratelli |first4=Diego |title=2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI) |chapter=A Class of Dielectric Resonator Antennas with Thermally Enhanced Performance |date=December 2021 |chapter-url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9704094 |pages=1175–1176 |doi=10.1109/APS/URSI47566.2021.9704094|isbn=978-1-7281-4670-6 |s2cid=246868331 |url=https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/6cf990df-9be1-4d6e-a4e3-9524150b2b00 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Dielectric Resonator Antenna Arrays for 5G Wireless Communications |date=2020-02-06 |journal=Microwave Journal |url=https://www.microwavejournal.com/articles/33434-dielectric-resonator-antenna-arrays-for-5g-wireless-communications |access-date=2023-07-10  |language=en}}</ref>

== Superformula ==
Gielis proposed the [[superformula]] in 2003.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Ortiz |first=Jesús Hamilton |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wHuQDwAAQBAJ&dq=who+is+johan+gielis+%3F&pg=PA221 |title=Wearable Technologies |date=2018-10-03 |publisher=BoD – Books on Demand |isbn=978-1-78984-003-2 |pages=221 |language=en |access-date=2023-07-05 |archive-date=2023-07-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705141142/https://books.google.com/books?id=wHuQDwAAQBAJ&newbks=0&printsec=frontcover&pg=PA221&dq=who+is+johan+gielis+%3F&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Superformula|superfomula]] is a generalization of the [[superellipse]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Gielis |first=J. |date=2003-03-01 |title=A generic geometric transformation that unifies a wide range of natural and abstract shapes |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.3732/ajb.90.3.333 |journal=American Journal of Botany |language=en |volume=90 |issue=3 |pages=333–338 |doi=10.3732/ajb.90.3.333 |pmid=21659124 |bibcode=2003AmJB...90..333G |issn=0002-9122 |access-date=2023-07-05 |archive-date=2023-07-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705141144/https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.3732/ajb.90.3.333 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He suggested that it allows for the creation of shapes that can mimic natural forms such as flowers, shells, and other intricate structures. The mathematical equation combines elements of trigonometry and algebra to generate complex and visually appealing patterns.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> It also allowed for a generalization of minimal surfaces based on a more general notion of the energy functional and allowed for a generalized definition of the Laplacian,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Koiso |first1=Miyuki |last2=Palmer |first2=Bennett |date=February 2008 |title=Rolling construction for anisotropic Delaunay surfaces |url=https://msp.org/pjm/2008/234-2/pjm-v234-n2-p09-p.pdf |journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics |volume=234 |issue=2 |pages=345–378|doi=10.2140/pjm.2008.234.345 }}</ref> and the use of Fourier projection methods to solve boundary value problems.<ref name=":0" />  
: <math>
\frac{1}{r} =\sqrt[n_1]{\,\left| \frac{1}{a} \cos \left( \frac{m}{4} \phi \right) \right|^{n_2} + \left| \frac{1}{b} \sin \left( \frac{m}{4} \phi \right) \right|^{n_3}} </math>

: ''r'' -  distance from the center, ''Φ'' - Angle to the x-axis,  ''m'' - symmetry, ''n''<sub>1</sub>, ''n''<sub>2</sub>, ''n''<sub>3</sub>: - Form, ''a'', ''b'': - expansion (semi-axes)<ref>{{Cite book |last=Chattopadhyay |first=Sudipta |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=smqQDwAAQBAJ&dq=who+is+johan+gielis+%3F&pg=PA91 |title=Microstrip Antennas: Trends in Research on |date=2017-11-15 |publisher=BoD – Books on Demand |isbn=978-953-51-3601-9 |pages=91 |language=en |access-date=2023-07-05 |archive-date=2023-07-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705141105/https://books.google.com/books?id=smqQDwAAQBAJ&newbks=0&printsec=frontcover&pg=PA91&dq=who+is+johan+gielis+%3F&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

Gielis patented the synthesis of patterns generated by the superformula.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Espacenet – search results |url=https://worldwide.espacenet.com/patent/search?q=pn=EP1177529 |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=worldwide.espacenet.com |archive-date=2023-07-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230705141114/https://worldwide.espacenet.com/patent/search?q=pn=EP1177529 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Chamary">{{Cite web |last=Chamary |first=J. V. |title=Did 'No Man's Sky' Steal A Scientist's Superformula? |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jvchamary/2016/07/27/no-mans-sky-superformula/ |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=Forbes |language=en |archive-date=2023-05-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230525023903/https://www.forbes.com/sites/jvchamary/2016/07/27/no-mans-sky-superformula/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The superformula was used in [[No Man's Sky]], an action-adventure survival game developed and published by [[Hello Games]].<ref name="Chamary"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Palumbo |first=Alessio |date=2016-07-25 |title=No Man's Sky Is Not Using Gielis' Superformula, But Sean Murray Wants To "Chat Maths" with Him |url=https://wccftech.com/no-mans-sky-not-using-gielis-superformula-sean-murray-wants-chat-maths/ |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=Wccftech |language=en-US |archive-date=2022-12-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209022907/https://wccftech.com/no-mans-sky-not-using-gielis-superformula-sean-murray-wants-chat-maths/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The formula was also used in the Jewels of the Sea.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Max Seeger - Jewels of the sea |url=https://maxseeger.de/jewels-of-the-sea |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=maxseeger.de |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-03-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230326002120/https://maxseeger.de/jewels-of-the-sea |url-status=live }}</ref>
